result: In 6 female CFS vs 8 matched controls on incremental cycle ergometry, predicted VO2peak was lower (1331 vs 1990 ml), exhaustion came sooner (351 vs 715 s) at lower power (100 vs 163 W) with lower max HR (154 vs 186 bpm), and prefrontal NIRS oxygenation and tHb were lower.
reason: Independent small cohort showing the same direction for lower peak VO2 (predicted, not measured) and low peak HR; this is replication, not extension.

result: Prefrontal cortex HbO2, HHb, tHb and TOI (NIRS) were lower at maximal exercise and in recovery in 6 CFS vs 8 controls.
reason: Measures cerebral oxygenation by NIRS during exercise, not cerebral blood flow during head-up tilt; no atlas finding covers exercise cerebral oxygenation.

result: Cochrane review of 15 RCTs (1043 participants): CBT vs usual care reduced self-rated fatigue post-treatment (SMD -0.39, 95% CI -0.60 to -0.19; 6 studies, 373 participants; clinical response 40% vs 26%), but follow-up findings were inconsistent.
reason: Pre-PACE pooled RCT evidence of modest self-rated fatigue gains with CBT that do not hold consistently at follow-up, matching the finding's pattern.

result: In a population-based sample (58 CFS vs 104 controls, psychiatric disorders and cognition-affecting drugs excluded), CANTAB showed slower motor/reaction speed and impaired spatial working memory and recognition; impairment rates ranged from 20% vs 4.8% (five-choice movement time) to 27.8% vs 10.6% (SWM strategy).
reason: Independent population-based cohort replicating reaction-time and working-memory deficits with psychiatric confounders excluded.

result: Low-dose (0.5 mg) dexamethasone suppressed salivary cortisol equally in 18 CFS and 20 controls (80.4% vs 76.2%); only the comorbid-depression subgroup (n=9) hypersuppressed (89.0%).
reason: Tests the same dexamethasone suppression measure and finds no overall enhanced feedback.

result: Basal salivary cortisol output (0800-2000 h) was raised, not lowered, in 18 CFS patients vs 20 matched controls.
reason: Same measure (salivary cortisol) in the opposite direction; small sample, authors call it atypical.

result: Polysomnography in 26 CFS (12 without, 14 with fibromyalgia) vs 26 controls showed less total sleep, lower sleep efficiency and less REM, with no excess sleep apnoea or PLMD; morning-sleepier patients had shorter runs of uninterrupted sleep.
reason: Small independent PSG cohort replicating lower sleep efficiency and absence of a diagnosable sleep disorder.

result: In 39 patients with laboratory-confirmed acute parvovirus B19, a high pre-infection stress index was the main predictor of CFS/ME 1-3 years later (OR 25.7, 95% CI 1.7-121.9).
reason: Does not measure post-infective CFS rates across EBV/Q fever/RRV; it tests psychological predictors, which immune-sickness-behaviour says do not predict, so it contradicts that finding.

result: In an uncontrolled trial of 24 CFS patients walking within HR (RER=1.0) and duration limits, fatigue rose immediately and was back to baseline at 24 h, pain stayed raised at 24 h, 14 had a meaningful rise in bodily pain and 6 reported slight worsening.
reason: Measures the time course of symptoms after exertion over 24 h; adds the response under sub-threshold, limited exercise; uncontrolled and only 24 h of follow-up.

result: In 41 CFS vs 30 controls, augmentation index (AIx@75) was higher (22.5% vs 13.3%, p=0.002), as were CRP (2.58 vs 1.07 ug/ml) and 8-iso-PGF2alpha isoprostanes (470.7 vs 331.1 pg/ml); AIx correlated with logCRP (r=0.507).
reason: Measures arterial stiffness by pulse-wave analysis, not FMD or PORH; its raised-CRP result replicates immune-cytokine-meta and its isoprostanes support omics-redox; no atlas finding covers arterial stiffness.
